name: Streets and Alleys
description: Streets and Alleys (also known as Gaps or Lane) is a solitaire game played with a single 52-card deck. It is similar to Beleaguered Castle but with a different layout. The entire deck is dealt into 8 tableau piles (wings). The goal is to build up the four foundations from Ace to King by suit.

overview.description: Streets and Alleys (also known as Gaps or Lane) is a solitaire game played with a single 52-card deck. It is similar to Beleaguered Castle but with a different layout. The entire deck is dealt into 8 tableau piles (wings). The goal is to build up the four foundations from Ace to King by suit.

history.origins: Streets and Alleys is a member of the Fortress family of solitaire games and a close variant of Beleaguered Castle. Unlike Beleaguered Castle, the aces remain in the deck and are not set out as foundations at the start, making the game somewhat harder. It is documented in Bicycle Official Rules of Card Games (1999) and in Parlett's Penguin Book of Patience. The layout of eight tableau piles in two wings with four foundations between them has been standard in solitaire collections.
history.cultural: A game of pure skill (open information).

setup.players: Single player. A patience or solitaire game for one; all cards are laid out at the start with no hidden information.
setup.deck: One standard 52-card deck. The entire deck is dealt at the start into eight tableau piles; no draw pile remains.
setup.dealing: Shuffle and deal the entire deck into 8 tableau piles in two wings of four each, with four foundation spaces in between. The top four piles receive 7 cards each, the remaining four receive 6 each. All cards are dealt face up.
setup.equipment: One standard deck and table space for eight tableau piles and four foundations.

rules.objective: Move all 52 cards onto the four foundations. Build each foundation up in suit from Ace to King; the game is won when every card has been moved to the foundations.
rules.gameplay: Top cards of tableau piles are available. Build tableaus down in sequence regardless of suit or color. Build foundations up in suit from Ace to King. An empty tableau pile may be filled with any single available card. Move cards between tableaus and from tableaus to foundations until all 52 cards are on the foundations.
keyRules: Tableau builds down regardless of suit.
Foundations build up in suit from Ace.
Empty tableau may hold any one card.
Only the top card of each tableau is available.

strategy.basic: Prioritize emptying a pile. An empty pile is a powerful tool to swap cards. Dig for Aces immediately. Don't bury low cards under high cards unless necessary.
strategy.intermediate: The 'Reverse Build': If you have an empty column, you can reverse a sequence (e.g., move 4-3-2 to empty spots to get the 2 onto a foundation).
strategy.advanced: Lookahead: Since all cards are visible, check if moving a 7 will trap a needed 2. Plan 5-10 moves ahead.

variations.name: Beleaguered Castle
variations.description: Aces are removed from the deck and placed as the four foundations at start; the eight tableau piles receive six cards each. Otherwise same build rules.
